To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TAL-1 exerts stage- and lineage-selective effects on the hematopoietic differentiation/proliferative gene program, and that it is up- and not down-modulated in megakaryopoiesis and erythropoieses, respectively.

enforced tal-1 over-expression in human hematopoietic cells induces a stimulatory action on primitive erythroid and myelopoietic progenitors and on primitive hematopoietic precursors, whereas it exerts a selective blockade on granulopoiesic differentiation.

tal-1 over-expression induces a stimulatory and stage- and/or lineage-specific effect on the HPCs/HSCs gene programs, and that the tal-1 gene is a key regulator of human adult hematopoietic cell differentiation and proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a gene that is involved in the control of HPC/HSC proliferation and lineage-specific differentiation and is differentially expressed in the myeloid versus the erythroid/megakaryocytic lineage.
the identification of a new differentiation factor, which may be useful in the design of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of human anemia and thrombocytopenia.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the lineage- and developmental stage-specific effects of TAL-1 on hematopoiesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tal-1 is a key gene in the control of the HPC/HPC/HSC differentiation program, which is differentially modulated in different stages and lineages of hematopoiesis.
enforced tal-1 over-expression induces a selective stimulatory effect on early erythroid and myelopoietic progenitors, whereas a partial blockade of granulocytic differentiation is observed.
TAL-1 is a stage- and lineage-dependent regulator of HPC/HSC proliferation, differentiation and self-renewal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
enforced expression of TAL-1 in HPC/HSCs causes a selective stimulatory effect on erythroid and primitive HPCs and a selective inhibitory effect on granulopoiesic differentiation.

TAL-1 is a transcription factor that, in a stage- and lineage-dependent manner, exerts a stimulatory effect on erythroid and primitive HPCs and a selective inhibitory action on the granulopoiesic differentiation program.
TAL-1 is a key factor in the regulation of HPC/HSC proliferation and differentiation programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tal-1 is a key factor in regulating the balance among different HPC/HSC progenitors and their differentiation programs.

tal-1 is a key regulator of HPC/HSC gene programs and that it can be exploited to modulate HPC/HSC proliferation and differentiation in vitro and, possibly, in vivo, in order to achieve a better control on hematopoiesis and its disorders.
tal-1 is a critical regulator of HPC/HSC fate and that its expression is differentially regulated during the myeloid lineage commitment.
